description: This is a terracotta oil lamp, likely of Roman origin, featuring a decorative relief on its discus. The relief depicts a figure, possibly a god or hero, in dynamic pose, surrounded by flowing drapery or natural elements. The lamp has a typical shape with a rounded body, a nozzle for the wick, and a handle. The central discus is deeply molded, creating a striking visual effect. The terracotta material gives it a warm, earthy tone. There is a dark, reflective surface in the oil reservoir, indicating it may have held oil. The overall craftsmanship suggests it was an object of both utility and artistic expression in its time.
